Subject: Post-call: VPC performance & latency SLO follow-up (ZenMed)

Hi Alice 

Thanks again for the call earlier. Quick recap and next steps so we have the performance criteria captured for the Proof-of-Concept (PoC):

Summary of SLOs we discussed:
- P95 generation latency <= 150ms for short prompts (<=256 tokens)
- Tail latency (P99) target <= 300ms for interactive flows
- Sustained throughput target: 1200 requests/minute across the service
- Concurrency target: support bursts up to 200 concurrent connections
- Streaming: support token-by-token streaming with <50ms inter-token latency

Network/architecture notes you mentioned:
- ZenMed wants Redwood Private in their VPC with peering/VPN to the inference subnet
- Internal latency budget from app tier to inference endpoint: ~20ms RTT
- Egress rules: limited to whitelisted IP ranges; no NAT for user data

Next steps / asks from our side:
1) Please share the VPC CIDRs, any transit gateway / peering topology diagrams, and the list of IPs we should expect to peer with.
2) Can you confirm expected concurrency patterns (steady vs spiky) and busiest hour QPS?
3) If possible, run a short connectivity check (ping/traceroute) to the candidate endpoint subnet and attach results - will help us validate network path and estimate added latency.

I'll loop in our Solutions/Network folks (marissa_cole and marcus_lin) to propose a short test plan and checklist. Attached is a lightweight network checklist and the PoC test matrix we usually run.

Proposed schedule: run the network checks this week, then we can schedule a 60-minute NetOps-to-NetOps call next week to configure peering and run an initial streaming latency test.

Thanks,
Jordan

Hi Alice / team - thanks for the diagram and the concurrency details. Quick tech checklist and proposed shallow validation steps from Redwood Net/Infra side:

1) Connectivity and topology
- Preferred: VPC peering where supported (lower NAT/egress overhead) - VPN is OK if peering not available.
- Please provide: peer VPC ID or VPN endpoint, ASN (if using TGW/BGP), and exact CIDRs to be whitelisted.
- We will provide a candidate endpoint (internal IP) to run traceroute/ping + MTU. Expect ~2-4ms added inside cloud region, plan for ~10-25ms additional depending on transit.

2) Firewall / Inspection
- If TLS inspection or DPI is in path, please flag it - these can add variable latency (~5-40ms).

3) Test matrix (quick PoC scope)
- Step A (connectivity): ping/traceroute/MTU from app subnet to provided endpoint; capture 10 samples.
- Step B (streaming latency): run 10 short streaming sessions (token-by-token) and capture inter-token latencies; target inter-token <50ms.
- Step C (throughput): run 5-minute spike to 2k req/min and monitor drop/queue behavior.
- Step D (tail latency): run steady-state 60-minute test at expected peak (~1,500 req/min) and capture P95/P99.

4) Data/egress and security
- Confirm whether traffic must egress via a NAT gateway with source IP translation or if we can peer directly. For whitelisting we will need the final egress range if NAT is used.

5) Scheduling
- Proposed slots: Tue 14 Dec 2026 16:00-17:00 PT or Wed 15 Dec 09:00-10:00 PT for NetOps-to-NetOps. Please confirm availability.

Deliverables from Redwood if you approve the PoC scope:
- Candidate endpoint IPs and whitelisted egress list
- Test harness scripts (iperf/streaming client) and a shared results CSV template (we will run and collect results)
- Post-test summary with latency histograms and recommendations (batching, KV cache hints, or quantization suggestions if we see performance concerns)

Alice - if you can drop the peer details and preferred slot, we'll get the test harness to you and set up the call.

Thanks - Marissa
